newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds post more gains, trade subdued.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds post more gains, trade subdued.

text.p: Argentine bonds managed to crawl higher again in the afternoon Friday to finish yet another session with solid price rises.

The market started with very low activity and even though the early closure of the U.S. Treasuries market kept activity at a minimum through the session there were enough buyers to generate gains in the afternoon, said a trader.
The FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/2 to 89-1/8, while the the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.15 to 125.25.
Traders said this week's rally could continue in coming days but Monday's session will be dull because of the holiday in the U.S. Treasuries market.
Analysts at Banco Rio said the placement of the awaited Argentine $2.0 billion global bond split between a five- and a 20-year issue will secure that the market's mood remains upbeat.

"If the cut-off yield is 11.375 percent (475 basis points over 20-year Treasuries) or less, bond yields, especially long duration ones, should continue falling," said Banco Rio in an investor note. The bond is expected to be placed in coming days.
Call money rates rose to 5.78 percent from 5.53 percent.
